  "name": "AI: spider rig -- Lazer is ~90% of the bot's deaths; reposition instead of sparing",
  "desc": "Follow-up from card 2c74d5b7, which tried the obvious lever and measured it as a net loss.

THE STANDING FINDING. On the spider rig (?level=Level2&spiderboss, Very_Hard, no ?invuln) the
killer histogram is overwhelmingly one entry: Lazer 49 of ~61 deaths, i.e. ~90%. Every other
cause is single digits. The bot is being killed by the big UFOs' beams -- the same beams it
deliberately invites, because only a Lazer hurts the SpiderBoss and a big UFO fires one 6x as
often as a small one.

WHAT WAS ALREADY TRIED AND REFUTED (do not re-run it). Sparing MORE big UFOs so the boss dies
sooner, via a reduced engage radius (?aibigufopx=, capped at 2 spared). Seeds 1-8 x2, N=16,
paired, directional:

  arm                deaths (paired)   victories   win@    Lazer kills   mean alive
  off (shipped)      3.81              6/16        158s    49            1.32
  capped at 250      +0.94 +- 1.09     7/16        219s    68            1.36
  capped at 300      +1.19 +- 1.23     4/16        112s    68            1.40
  UNCAPPED at 250    +1.50 +- 0.89     6/16        241s    72            1.46

The counter moved as designed and the fight did not follow. It bakes to 0 (off). Also bounded:
the radius is behaviourally inert above the bot's own reach (351px bullet travel + the target's
hull credit from card bb949dd9 = ~400px for a big UFO), so that lever has ~100..400px of range
and every value in it loses.

THE HYPOTHESIS THIS CARD IS FOR: the problem is not HOW MANY guns are alive, it is WHERE THE
BOT STANDS relative to them. A Lazer is aimed at the player's position at fire time, has a
2500ms visible windup (UFO.AiChargingLazer), and then sits still for >=3250ms. That is a lot of
warning for a ~90% death cause.

TWO UNTRIED DIRECTIONS, either or both:
  1. The beam-avoidance MAGNITUDES on this rig specifically. Card 2248e5eb re-measured them
     against the 2008 originals and restored 150px / strength 4 / no sidestep -- a good result
     on the rigs it swept, but it did not have this card's killer histogram in front of it, and
     ?ailazerpx= / ?ailazerstrength= / ?ailazerdodge= are all still live seams.
  2. A POSITIONAL term that keeps the ship off the invited beam's line -- i.e. treat a charging
     big UFO's aim ray as a repellent during its windup, rather than only reacting to the beam
     once it exists. The AI's own doctrine says threat awareness belongs in the repellent's
     SHAPE (card ada9e839), and card e425781b's velocity cones are the precedent for an
     anisotropic one.

INSTRUMENTS THAT ALREADY EXIST, so this card starts with measurement rather than plumbing:
  - killers=Lazer:<n> in ?aibench (the headline number above)
  - bigufo= / bigspared= / bigalive= (card 2c74d5b7) -- the surviving-executioner census

    deaths cluster on beam lines
  - ?ailazerpx= ?ailazerstrength= ?ailazerdodge= ?aibigufopx= -- the seams
  - python tools/sim/ai_sweep.py --rig spider

GATE: N=60 paired (seeds 1-30 x2), spider rig. Lazer kills down, deaths flat-or-better, and
check level1/spacedodge/crazygame for collateral -- the beam terms are global, not spider-only.",

  "desc": "Split out of card fd126847 (the station-seek pingpong), which fixed a DIFFERENT oscillation on the same complaint.\n\nTHE OBSERVATION (pre-change -- see the re-measure step below before believing it):\nOn `?level=Level3&brainboss&aiplayer&aibench&invuln&noattract&seed=1&difficulty=Very_Hard` the ship traces a closed loop for hundreds of ticks -- 227px of path per second for 3px of net travel, amplitude ~38px, period 20 ticks, `revs/s` 8.5, `turn` 178 deg/s. `?aiseeklog` attributes every tick of it to `kind=boss dist~300px gate=on`, i.e. the BOSS APPROACH attractor, not the station seek and not a deadzone.\n\nSUSPECTED MECHANISM (not proven): a curl limit cycle. Every radial threat repellent is emitted at `MyMath.VectorToAngle(pos - baddy) + dodgeAngle` (+-PI/16 for slots 0/1), while the boss attractor points straight at the boss. At the crossing the two equal magnitudes therefore do NOT cancel to zero but to `2*w*sin(dodge/2)` -- a purely TRANSVERSE residual, which is a vortex, not an equilibrium. `PlayerShip.BossApproachExponent`'s comment already states this for slots 2/3 (\"such a ship orbits instead\") and argues slot 0's 0.13 residual falls under the 0.2 noise floor; the trace says something is circling at slot 0 anyway.\n\nFIRST STEP -- RE-MEASURE, DO NOT TRUST THE ABOVE:\nCard bb949dd9 (merged after this observation was taken) moves the boss standoff anchor into the floored regime on brainboss, so the equilibrium measured here no longer exists as-is. Re-run the trace on current main FIRST:\n\n  dotnet build web/EvilAliensWeb -c Debug && dotnet build tools/headless -c Debug\n  tools/headless/bin/Debug/net8.0/eahl.exe --flags \"?level=Level3&brainboss&aiplayer&aibench&invuln&noattract&seed=1&difficulty=Very_Hard&aiseeklog\" --frames 800 --nodraw\n\nand read the `[aiseek]` lines. If the cycle is gone, close this card as fixed-in-passing (record the numbers either way). `python tools/sim/ai_seek_trace.py --rig Level3 --dump` prints the same rows reduced.\n\nIF IT IS STILL THERE, the tools are already in place: `?aiseeklog` for attribution, `logic_probe`'s ProbeAiBossApproach for the band, `ai_sweep.py` for the verdict (N=60 paired, per the measurement bar). Note the band's width bound assumes the two forces are COLLINEAR -- that assumption is what to attack, and rotating the attractor to match dodgeAngle changes what \"aim at the boss\" means for the human-facing seats too, so it is not a free fix.\n\nNOT a duplicate of bb949dd9 (how NEAR the boss the ship parks) or 5c89e4e6 (target leading): this is about whether it parks at all.",

        "text": "ANSWER TO THE CARD'S QUESTION: mostly no -- and the one exception is the culprit.\n\nAudited DoAIMove against src_decompiled/EvilAliens/PlayerShip.cs:\n  * the four generic screen-edge repulsions (steerRange 150, strengths 0..4, PowerCurve exp 2, the 560px Floor bottom) -- 2008 VERBATIM (lines 1070-1113)\n  * the powerup's own pull, its 150px reach and the 0.8 seek weight -- 2008 VERBATIM (lines 995-1015, 1060-1068)\n  * the top-edge 'UFOs spawn here' band (170px / strength 20) -- a PORT ADDITION with no 2008 counterpart at all\n\nSo 'I'm pretty sure this used to work fine' is right, and the thing that changed is the band the port added.\n\nWHY IT BLOCKED PICKUPS. maxSteerStrength is 4, and 4 is ALSO the ceiling of the powerup approach pull. Card 2248e5eb's deaths cost for dropping the band outright was +0.67..+0.88, which is INVISIBLE at this sweep's ~0.8 SEM. So a value that merely looks flat on deaths at N=16 is not evidence of being safe; the conservative pick is the highest strength recovering most of the pickup gain, which is likelier to survive N=60. Removal outright stays refuted by 2248e5eb.\n\nA tuning change WITH a paired measurement (N=16 here, N=60 at the scoring gate).\n\nSEAMS / VERIFICATION:\n  * ?aitopedgecompose=0 restores the pre-card placement -- deliberate bug reproduction, in DebugFlags.Active, one-way like ?netstaleguard=0\n  * [aitopedge] placement: composed|post-smoothing, printed from INSIDE each branch (the flags dump reports only the parse)\n  * logic_probe ProbeAiTopEdge -- profile, the DERIVED exclusion height (it scans the real function and cross-checks the closed form, so the 20->12 flip re-derived 129->102 unaided), the flag's one-way spelling\n  * tools/headless/probes/ai_top_edge.txt + ai_top_edge_precard.txt, both mutation-tested twice\n\nTWO NEAR-MISSES WORTH KNOWING (both caught and fixed): the placement report first read the predicate rather than the branch taken, so inverting the dispatch left the probe pair GREEN on the very mutation it exists to catch; and a single shared report latch meant a build applying the band at BOTH sites (double strength) printed exactly a healthy build's line. Hence per-branch names and one latch per site -- both recorded in the probe headers.\n\nClean build, logic_probe ALL PASS, 60/60 headless probes green. Commits e4831f0 + d483a3f.",

      "data": {
        "text": "DONE — merged as PR #321 (merge b4d9a9f; work c80d58b, main-merge 7522015).

VERDICT UP FRONT: the ticket's suggestion was IMPLEMENTED, MEASURED ACROSS ITS WHOLE USABLE
BAND, AND DECLINED ON THE NUMBERS. What ships is the instrument that can answer the question;
the behaviour change bakes OFF behind a seam. The ticket's implied "more UFOs survive" outcome
is deliberately UNMET, because every configuration that achieved it measured as a net loss.

THE PREMISE IS CORRECT, and was checked before anything was written. Only a Lazer hurts the
SpiderBoss (SpiderBoss.CollidesWith), a BIG UFO fires one 6x as often as a small one (UFO.Update:
0.0009/ms against 0.00015), and the boss's whole pool is 5 * DifficultyFactorized(0.75). So the
surviving big-UFO population really is the fight's clock, and the bot really was shortening its
own guns' lifespan. The reasoning in the card is sound; it is the OUTCOME that does not follow.

ANSWER TO "PERHAPS REDUCE RADIUS WHERE IT SHOOTS AT BIG UFOs?" -- THE LEVER IS BOUNDED, and this
is the durable half of the finding. The bot never fires past its own reach, so any radius at or
above that is behaviourally INERT: nothing is shot that far, so declining to shoot it changes
nothing. That reach is 351px of bullet travel PLUS the target's hull credit (card bb949dd9,
which landed alongside this one), measured ~400px for a big UFO -- runs at 400 / 420 / 450
produce an identical world. So "reduce the radius" has roughly 100..400px to work in, not an
open range. And every value in that range loses.

MEASURED (eahl, spider rig ?level=Level2&spiderboss, Very_Hard, ?invuln OFF, seeds 1-8 x2,
paired). N=16 -- DIRECTIONAL, below the repo's N=60 floor, stated as such. The sign was
consistent across all three radii and both variants, which is why it was enough to decide:

  arm                deaths (paired)   victories   win@    Lazer kills   mean alive
  off (=0, shipped)  3.81              6/16        158s    49            1.32
  capped at 250      +0.94 +- 1.09     7/16        219s    68            1.36
  capped at 300      +1.19 +- 1.23     4/16        112s    68            1.40
  UNCAPPED at 250    +1.50 +- 0.89     6/16        241s    72            1.46

Read honestly: the counter moves EXACTLY as designed (mean alive up, and big UFOs alive at boss
death 2.67 -> 3.50 uncapped) and the fight does not follow. Neither deaths diff clears 2 SEM, so
this is "not better", NOT "significantly worse". But nothing here is an improvement to ship.

WHY IT LOSES, which is the useful part: the beams the bot is inviting are aimed AT IT, and it
was already dying to them. Lazer is ~90% of deaths on this rig (16 of 18 in the first baseline,
49 of ~61 across the full sweep) -- far and away the largest killer. Past the second beam
platform each extra one costs more dodging than it buys boss damage. The problem is not HOW MANY
guns are alive, it is WHERE THE BOT STANDS relative to them. Filed as follow-up card 65211515
("spider rig -- Lazer is ~90% of the bot's deaths; reposition instead of sparing"), naming the
two untried directions: the beam-avoidance magnitudes on this rig specifically (?ailazerpx= /
?ailazerstrength= / ?ailazerdodge=, live seams that card 2248e5eb set without this histogram in
front of it), and a positional term treating a charging big UFO's aim ray as a repellent during
its 2500ms windup.

WHAT SHIPS.

1. THE OBSERVABLE (the deliverable). Three run-wide AiBench fields, sampled inside DoAIFire's
   EXISTING baddy scan so the bench adds no second pass, appended to Line() and Row() with
   nothing reordered, no-op without ?aibench:
     bigufo=    mean big UFOs alive per tick while a spider boss lives  -- the OUTCOME
     bigspared= mean deliberately spared per tick                       -- the DECISION
     bigalive=  count at the instant the boss died, -1 if it never did  -- the card's literal ask
   COMPARE ARMS ON bigspared, not bigufo: the outcome swings 1.24..1.95 across seeds on ONE arm,
   which straddles the whole effect, while the decision separates cleanly (0.45 shipped against
   0.67-0.86 with the gate on). bigalive uses -1 rather than 0 so "never finished" and "finished
   with none left" stay distinguishable in a sweep's mean. ai_sweep.py prints all three,
   suppressed on the six rigs with no spider boss.

2. THE MECHANISM, reachable but off. ?aibigufopx=<px> spares ONE more big UFO beyond that radius,
   capped at PlayerShip.BigUfoSpareCap (2 total, spare-one rule included).
   DefaultBigUfoEngagePx = 0. The cap is not a flag on purpose -- a second knob would let a sweep
   wander back to the uncapped arm, which is the worst of the four.

3. The spare rule is factored out of DoAIFire into SelectSparedBigUfos so it can be read as DATA
   at one instant over one world (eaBigUfoSpare(px) evaluates the gate at px AND at 0 in the same
   tick). Not tidiness: running one arm and then the other INSIDE a fight compares two different
   screens, and doing so INVERTED the true result on seed 5. That is also why the probes are a
   cross-process pair rather than one sequential script.

TWO BUGS WRITTEN AND CAUGHT DURING THE CARD, both now pinned: the gate-off guard (`room` is a
length, so a bare `sparedFarRoom > engagePx` spares at EVERY radius including zero -- the exact
inverse of the pre-card build it restores), and a first probe design that PASSED under mutation
because `expect` scans the whole window and AiBench prints every 10 sim-s, so an early transient
satisfied both bands. Fixed with a second `mark` before the final report.

VERIFICATION: clean build (no new warnings); logic_probe ALL PASS (38 knobs, new ?aibigufopx
rejection row; its header count is now DERIVED from the table rather than a literal that had
already drifted); 63/63 headless probes including T1/T2/T3's. New probes ai_bigufo_gate.txt /
ai_bigufo_gate_off.txt / ai_bigufo_death.txt, mutation-tested -- re-baking the default to 250
turns gate_off red while gate stays green. THE N=60 GATE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT RUN; that is the
later scoring pass's job, and every number above is small-N.

MERGE (fourth of four siblings): both ProbeAiFlagRejection rows survive (aigunhull + aibigufopx),
and the merged DoAIFire predicate carries BOTH the spare exclusions and bb949dd9's per-candidate
hull-credited reach test. Two semantic interactions, not just textual: the "inert above 351px"
finding became ~400px (hull credit), corrected everywhere it was written; and
ai_bigufo_death.txt was re-pinned seed 2 -> 1 because the reach change moved the world enough
that seed 2 stopped killing the boss inside budget. Its header now says the seed is a rig
parameter to re-pick, not a constant.",
